text: Did the eraser leave the message by removing a layer or substance from the sheet, thereby revealing the message underneath?
Did A use the eraser as a stamp or marking tool, depositing something onto the paper to form the message?
Did A write the message by pressing the eraser into the paper, leaving indentations that could be read by touch or under suitable lighting?
Did A use friction or heat from the eraser to form the message on the paper?
Was the message conveyed by the eraser itself—for example, by its shape, markings, or position on the blank sheet—rather than being written onto the paper?
Did A use the eraser to cast a shadow or otherwise alter the light falling on the paper so that the message became visible?
Did using the eraser cause a separate tool or mechanism to write or display the message on the paper?
Did A use the eraser to activate an electronic device that then displayed or printed the message on the paper?
Did the eraser mechanically trigger a writing instrument, such as a pencil or pen, to move across the paper and write the message?
Did the eraser trigger another person or animal to write the message on the paper?
Did A use the eraser to trigger a non-electronic machine or mechanism that printed or otherwise formed the message on the paper?
Did A use the eraser to remove or alter something other than the blank sheet, and did that action cause the separate tool or mechanism to produce the message?
Did A use the eraser to erase a mark or writing on a separate surface, and did that erasure trigger the mechanism that produced the message?
Did A use the eraser to remove a non-written substance—such as dirt, paint, or a coating—from a separate object or surface?
